chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Nawfaly, raised it to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed by a camel shepherd, so he sent to him to quench him, but he said, 'As for what is in their udders, it is for the morning, and as for what is in our containers, it is for the evening.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Allah! Increase his wealth and his children.'

Then he passed by a sheep shepherd, so he sent for him to quench him. So he milked for him whatever was in its udders, and poured what was in his container into the container of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and sent a sheep to him, saying: 'This is what is with us, and if you love that we increase it for you, we will increase it for you.' He said, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Allah! Grant him sufficiency (al-kafaf).'

One of his companions said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah! You supplicated for the one who repulsed you with a supplication which the majority of us love, and you supplicated for the one who relieved you of your need with a supplication which we all dislike.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, what is little and sufficient is better than what is abundant and diverting. O Allah! Grant Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad sufficiency (al-kafaf).'

key_terms.الكَفَاف: sufficiency, moderate provision, enough to meet needs without excess

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'al-kafaf' in the hadith of the two shepherds?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Prophetic wisdom in distinguishing between material abundance and spiritual sufficiency, a key theme in Shia ethics regarding *al-Kafaf* (moderate provision). The Prophet’s specific prayer for the generous shepherd to have 'enough' rather than 'more' reflects the belief that excessive wealth can become a distraction (*lahw*) from divine remembrance, a nuance highlighted by the companion's query. This narrative underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on contentment and the spiritual dangers of accumulation, linking material state directly to spiritual focus.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad Al Nowfaly, 
(It has been narrated) raising it to Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasoool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> passed by a camel shepherd, so he<sup>saww</sup> sent to him to quench him<sup>saww</sup>, but he said, ‘As for what is in their udders, so it is for their morning, and as for what is in our containers, so it is for their evening’.
So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Increase his wealth and his children’.

Then he<sup>saww</sup> passed by a sheep shepherd. So he<sup>saww</sup> sent for him to quench him<sup>saww</sup>. So he milked for him<sup>saww</sup> whatever was in its udders, and added to whatever was in his container into the container of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and sent a sheep over to him<sup>saww</sup> and said: ‘This is what is with us, and if you<sup>saww</sup> so love it that we increase it for you<sup>saww</sup>, we shall increase it for you<sup>saww</sup>’. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Grace him at the subsistence level’.

So one of his<sup>saww</sup> companions said to him<sup>saww</sup>, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! You<sup>saww</sup> supplicated for the one who repulsed you<sup>saww</sup> with a supplication which the generality of us would love, and you<sup>saww</sup> supplicated to the one who relieved you<sup>saww</sup> of your<sup>saww</sup> need with a supplication which we all would dislike’. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘What is little and just enough is better than what is more and diverting. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Grace Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> and the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, the subsistence’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Ya’qub ibn Yazid from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Nawfali in a marfu’ manner from Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah once passed by a shepherd of camels and asked him for a drink and he said, ‘The milk in their udder is for the morning drink of the people of the village and the milk in the containers is for their evening drink.’ The Messenger of Allah then prayed, ‘O Lord, give him many children and much wealth.’

The Messenger of Allah then passed by a shepherd of sheep and sent his people to ask him for a drink. He milked them and poured it from his milk container altogether in the container for the Messenger of Allah. Along with all the milk he also sent a sheep for him, saying, ‘This is what we have and we can bring you more if you like.’ The Imam said, ‘The Messenger of Allah prayed for him, “O Lord, give him sustenance adequate only for his bare necessities.”

A certain man of his companion then asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, how is it that you prayed for the shepherd who refused to give you any milk in such a way that we all love. However, for the one who readily provided what you asked, you prayed for him with a prayer that we all dislike?’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘The little thing that is adequate is better than a great deal that diverts one’s mind (from Allah). O Lord, grant to Muhammad and the family of Muhammad only that much which is adequate for them.’”
